verdict.rationale: LangGraph's interrupt() mechanism explicitly pauses graph execution at specific points to await external (human) input before resuming via Command, and checkpointers/persistence are documented as supporting human-in-the-loop workflows and state modification at any point — this is the standard pattern for gating sensitive tool calls behind approval. Community commentary independently confirms LangGraph's state-machine/time-travel design is specifically valued for human-in-the-loop approval and correction use cases. Missing for 10: a first-party worked example showing interrupt placed specifically before a tool-call node for approval (only generic interrupt-point docs are shown) and independent hands-on validation of that exact pattern.
